label: Figure 5
title: Formula and pass-through programmes: who receives the federal money, and whom a non-profit applies to (as the federal pages state it, read October 4–5, 2026)

columns.label: Whom a non-profit or local organisation applies to
What the federal source says about applying locally
Bodies at each level, where stated

caption: The table lists the forty-four programme records that carry a pass-through field or the status formula: the twenty-eight on the formula route, eight more that send money through an intermediary, and eight formula grants paid straight to named colleges or experiment stations. Two federal texts say in so many words that the agency deals with no non-profit directly: HUD's page states that it gives no Community Development Block Grant assistance directly to non-profits, and FEMA's notice that non-profits may not apply directly for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program [1292](#cite:1292) [1320](#cite:1320). The records say the same of SAMHSA's substance use block grant, HRSA's Title V and the Education Department's 21st Century Community Learning Centers [1130](#cite:1130) [1168](#cite:1168) [1399](#cite:1399). The longest chain the records state is the Older Americans Act's: 56 state agencies on aging, 618 area agencies on aging and nearly 20,000 local service providers [1260](#cite:1260). Each row ends at the body named, because the guide's scope ends there; no state's own process is described. No record that met the rule was left out.
how_to_read: Read across a row. The first two columns name the programme and its federal owner, the third says who receives the federal award, and the fourth names the body you would approach. The fifth gives the federal source's own words in quotation marks, or a short paraphrase. A blank in the chain column means the record gives no count of bodies. "Does not describe the local process" means the federal pages read are silent on how a local organisation applies; it does not mean that no process exists. Where the fourth column begins "None named", the formula pays the listed institutions directly and there is no intermediary.

explain.text: The body that holds the federal award and passes money on. VOCA victim assistance grants go by formula to the states and territories, which make subgrants to local community-based organisations and public agencies [1280](#cite:1280).
The amount is set by a rule, not by a contest between applicants. ACL describes formula grants as ongoing programmes that need no application or competition [1259](#cite:1259).

The count of bodies at each level, in the record's own wording. Most rows give the first level only, and the bodies counted differ by programme: OVC's FY 2026 chart lists 56 jurisdictions, the 50 states, the District of Columbia and 5 territories [1470](#cite:1470).

explain.on: Single State Agency, State Administrative Agency
explain.text: The state body has a different name in each programme. SAMHSA calls the State Substance Abuse Agency the Single State Agency, and under the Nonprofit Security Grant Program a non-profit applies to its State Administrative Agency [1219](#cite:1219) [1320](#cite:1320).

explain.on: None named: the record's route is direct
explain.text: Eight rows are formula grants with no intermediary. Title III Part B pays each eligible historically Black college or university a yearly grant worked out by formula, and an institution on the list in 34 CFR 608.2 files the application itself [1602](#cite:1602) [1649](#cite:1649).

source: Values come from the guide's programme records and from the federal pages, notices, statutes and regulations those records cite, as published on the dates read, October 4–5, 2026. Wording and counts are as the records give them. Nothing was restated as a plain number and no cell holds a calculated figure. Rows follow the order of the formula route, then the other pass-through records, then the direct formula records.

rows.programme: Community Mental Health Services Block Grant (MHBG)
rows.money_goes_to: States and territories, by formula
rows.nonprofit_door: The State Mental Health Authority, which submits the application and plan
rows.federal_page_says: The state provides services "only through appropriate, qualified community programs"; no federal page read says how a provider applies to a state
rows.chain: 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands and 6 Pacific jurisdictions

rows.programme: Substance Use Prevention, Treatment, and Recovery Services Block Grant (SUBG)
rows.money_goes_to: States, territories and one tribal entity, by formula
rows.nonprofit_door: The State Substance Abuse Agency, which SAMHSA also calls the Single State Agency; it funds public and non-profit providers
rows.federal_page_says: A state may give financial assistance only to public or non-profit private entities; the state plan is made public for comment
rows.chain: 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, 6 Pacific jurisdictions and 1 tribal entity

rows.programme: State Opioid Response Grants (SOR)
rows.money_goes_to: State substance use agencies and territories
rows.nonprofit_door: The Single State Agency for substance use services in each state; providers are funded by the state
rows.federal_page_says: "Eligibility is limited to Single State Agencies (SSAs) and territories."
rows.chain: 59 expected awards in the 2024 listing

rows.programme: Title V Maternal and Child Health Services Block Grant
rows.money_goes_to: States and jurisdictions, which apply each year
rows.nonprofit_door: The state's Title V agency
rows.federal_page_says: "States decide how to use the funding."; the page does not describe how a local organization applies

rows.programme: Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program (MIECHV)
rows.money_goes_to: The 50 states and 6 jurisdictions
rows.nonprofit_door: The state or jurisdiction that holds the award; local home visiting agencies are funded by the state
rows.federal_page_says: "Nonprofit organizations currently funded are eligible to apply if the state/jurisdiction does not apply."; the forecast does not describe subawards
rows.chain: 50 states and 6 jurisdictions; 56 awards in the FY 2027 forecast

rows.programme: Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program Parts A and B (grants to metropolitan areas, states and territories)
rows.money_goes_to: Part A: the chief elected official of the cities and counties most affected by HIV. Part B: states and territories
rows.nonprofit_door: Part A: the chief elected official's office or the lead agency it names, guided by a planning council or planning body. Part B: the state or territory
rows.federal_page_says: does not describe the local process
rows.chain: Part A: 23 Eligible Metropolitan Areas and 28 Transitional Grant Areas. Part B: the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands and six territories

rows.programme: Public Health Infrastructure Grant (Strengthening U.S. Public Health Infrastructure, Workforce, and Data Systems)
rows.money_goes_to: State, territorial and large local health departments and three national partner organizations
rows.nonprofit_door: The state, territorial or local health department that holds the award
rows.federal_page_says: The CDC page states no rule on subawards and does not describe subawards to community organizations
rows.chain: 107 health departments (all 50 states, Washington D.C., 8 territories and freely associated states, and 48 large localities) and 3 national partners

rows.programme: Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program
rows.money_goes_to: Approved states, in each of fiscal years 2026 to 2030
rows.nonprofit_door: The state agency that holds the state's award; rural providers and organizations take part through their state's approved plan
rows.federal_page_says: "Only the 50 U.S. states are eligible to receive an RHT Program award"; the CMS page read does not state subaward rules
rows.chain: the 50 states

rows.programme: Child Care and Development Fund (Child Care and Development Block Grant)
rows.money_goes_to: States, territories and tribes, which submit plans every three years
rows.nonprofit_door: The state, territorial or tribal child care lead agency named in the CCDF plan
rows.federal_page_says: Subsidies reach providers as "certificates (vouchers), or grants and contracts with providers"

rows.programme: Community Services Block Grant
rows.money_goes_to: States, territories and tribes
rows.nonprofit_door: The state CSBG office and the local Community Action Agency; ACF links a "Find Your CAA" tool
rows.federal_page_says: States pass no less than 90 percent to local eligible entities; how an organisation not already an eligible entity obtains CSBG money is not stated
rows.chain: more than 1,000 local agencies and tribal organisations

rows.programme: Family Violence Prevention and Services Act formula grants to states and tribes
rows.federal_agency: ACF Office of Family Violence Prevention and Services (HHS)
rows.money_goes_to: States, territories and tribes
rows.nonprofit_door: The state or territory agency, or the tribe, that receives the FVPSA formula grant
rows.federal_page_says: By statute a subgrant may go to a local public agency or a non-profit private organisation, including faith-based and community-based organisations

rows.programme: Social Services Block Grant
rows.money_goes_to: States and territories, as a capped entitlement
rows.nonprofit_door: The state agency that administers SSBG
rows.federal_page_says: "States may provide services directly, or sub-allocate funds to local qualified providers."

rows.programme: Older Americans Act Title III - supportive services, nutrition and caregiver support
rows.money_goes_to: State agencies on aging, as formula funding
rows.nonprofit_door: The state agency on aging and the area agency on aging for the planning and service area
rows.federal_page_says: "Mandatory, or 'formula,' grants are on-going programs, which require no application or competition"
rows.chain: 56 state agencies on aging, 618 area agencies on aging, nearly 20,000 local service providers

rows.programme: Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) Victim Assistance formula grants
rows.federal_agency: DOJ Office for Victims of Crime
rows.money_goes_to: States and territories, by formula from the Crime Victims Fund
rows.nonprofit_door: The state VOCA victim assistance administrator; OVC lists state contacts on its State Support map at ovc.ojp.gov/states
rows.federal_page_says: States make subgrants to "local community-based organizations and public agencies that provide services directly to victims"
rows.chain: 56 states and territories in OVC's FY2026 chart

rows.programme: OVW STOP Violence Against Women Formula Grant Program
rows.federal_agency: DOJ Office on Violence Against Women
rows.money_goes_to: The state office named by each governor; each state or territory receives $600,000 and the rest is allotted by population
rows.nonprofit_door: The state office designated by the chief executive of the state to administer STOP funds; a non-profit victim service provider seeks a subgrant from that office
rows.federal_page_says: Only the designated state office may apply; "Subgrants to Tribes and to victim service providers for victim services are not subject to this match requirement."
rows.chain: 56 STOP awards in FY2025

rows.programme: Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Program
rows.money_goes_to: States, tribes and local governments; only the designated state administering agencies receive the state awards
rows.nonprofit_door: The state administering agency for JAG in each state, or the local government that holds a direct award
rows.federal_page_says: BJA's overview does not say whether a non-profit may receive a subaward; it directs local governments without a direct award to the state administering agency

rows.programme: OJJDP Title II Formula Grants Program
rows.federal_agency: DOJ Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention
rows.money_goes_to: The state agency named by the governor
rows.nonprofit_door: The designated state agency and its Juvenile Justice Specialist
rows.federal_page_says: "Only state agencies, designated by the Governor, are eligible to apply."; subgrants go to units of local government, local private agencies and Indian Tribes
rows.chain: 48 states, the District of Columbia and several territories in the FY2023 awards

rows.programme: Community Development Block Grant
rows.federal_agency: HUD Office of Community Planning and Development
rows.money_goes_to: Entitlement cities and urban counties, and states for smaller places
rows.nonprofit_door: The city, urban county or state that holds the CDBG grant
rows.federal_page_says: "HUD does not provide CDBG assistance directly to individuals, businesses, nonprofit or organizations or other non-governmental entities."
rows.chain: 49 States and Puerto Rico run the State CDBG Program for other areas

rows.programme: HOME Investment Partnerships Program
rows.federal_agency: HUD Office of Community Planning and Development
rows.money_goes_to: Participating jurisdictions (states and localities)
rows.nonprofit_door: The participating jurisdiction (state or local government) that holds the HOME grant
rows.federal_page_says: Part of each grant is set aside for qualified community-based non-profit housing groups; the rule reserves not less than 15 percent

rows.programme: Nonprofit Security Grant Program
rows.money_goes_to: The State Administrative Agency, the only eligible applicant, which submits the state's package to FEMA
rows.nonprofit_door: The State Administrative Agency, which sets its own earlier deadline for non-profits and scores their Investment Justifications
rows.federal_page_says: "Nonprofit organizations may NOT apply directly to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS)/FEMA."

rows.programme: WIOA Title I formula grants - Adult, Dislocated Worker and Youth
rows.money_goes_to: States and outlying areas, by statutory formula
rows.nonprofit_door: The state workforce agency and the local area's American Job Center network; ETA gives 1-877-US-2JOBS and the CareerOneStop site for local contacts
rows.federal_page_says: ETA's programme page does not describe how a local board selects service or training providers

rows.programme: Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC)
rows.money_goes_to: State educational agencies, by formula; each state runs its own competition
rows.nonprofit_door: The state educational agency; the Department's page lists each state's 21st CCLC contact
rows.federal_page_says: Local educational agencies, community-based organizations, Indian tribes or tribal organizations, other public or private entities and consortia may apply for a state's subgrants

rows.programme: Charter Schools Program, Grants to State Entities
rows.federal_agency: U.S. Department of Education (FY 2026 competition run by the Department of Labor)
rows.money_goes_to: A state entity: a state educational agency, a state charter school board, a governor, or a charter school support organization
rows.nonprofit_door: The state entity that holds the grant; it runs the State's charter school subgrant programme, and a school developer applies to it for a subgrant
rows.federal_page_says: The state entity makes subgrants to those opening or expanding charter schools in the State

rows.programme: NEA Partnership Agreement Grants (state arts agencies and regional arts organizations)
rows.money_goes_to: State and jurisdictional arts agencies and regional arts organizations
rows.nonprofit_door: The state or jurisdictional arts agency, or the regional arts organization
rows.federal_page_says: A subrecipient must provide a UEI; state agencies must decide on criteria that include artistic excellence and artistic merit
rows.chain: 56 state and jurisdictional arts agencies and six regional arts organizations

rows.programme: NEH Federal/State Partnership (state and jurisdictional humanities councils)
rows.money_goes_to: State and jurisdictional humanities councils, as general operating support grants
rows.nonprofit_door: The state or jurisdictional humanities council; NEH offers a contact list of the councils on its Federal/State Partnership page
rows.federal_page_says: Each council sets its own programmes and deadlines; NEH's page lists none
rows.chain: humanities councils in 56 states and jurisdictions

rows.programme: IMLS Grants to States (Library Services and Technology Act)
rows.federal_agency: Institute of Museum and Library Services
rows.money_goes_to: State Library Administrative Agencies, by a population-based formula
rows.nonprofit_door: The State Library Administrative Agency, through competitive subawards or cooperative agreements
rows.federal_page_says: Each agency either runs statewide services or makes competitive subawards to libraries, and sets its own subaward calendar
rows.chain: State Library Administrative Agencies of the 50 States, the District of Columbia, five territories and three Freely Associated States

rows.programme: AmeriCorps State and National Grants
rows.money_goes_to: By regulation one third goes to States by population formula, at least one third is competed among States, and the remainder is competed directly
rows.nonprofit_door: The State service commission, for the formula share and for the share competed among States; a non-profit may also apply under the competitive notice
rows.federal_page_says: The Grants.gov listing names non-profits among eligible applicants and says applicants apply through Grants.gov

rows.programme: 4-H and Cooperative Extension (through land-grant universities)
rows.money_goes_to: Land-grant institutions, through capacity grants to the states on statutory formulas
rows.nonprofit_door: The Cooperative Extension Service of the state's land-grant university
rows.federal_page_says: The page describes no direct NIFA grant to a community non-profit for 4-H

rows.programme: NIH IDeA Networks of Biomedical Research Excellence (INBRE)
rows.federal_agency: NIH National Institute of General Medical Sciences
rows.money_goes_to: The lead institution of one statewide network in each IDeA state and Puerto Rico
rows.nonprofit_door: The lead institution of the statewide INBRE network; a primarily undergraduate institution in an IDeA state takes part as a network institution
rows.federal_page_says: "funds statewide networks of higher education and research institutions in each IDeA-states and Puerto Rico to build biomedical research capacity"

rows.programme: HUD Section 4 Capacity Building for Community Development and Affordable Housing
rows.federal_agency: HUD Office of Community Planning and Development
rows.money_goes_to: Three national non-profits named in the statute
rows.nonprofit_door: Enterprise Community Partners, Local Initiatives Support Corporation and Habitat for Humanity International, each of which runs its own process for the local groups it supports
rows.federal_page_says: "Affiliates and local offices of these organizations and their community partners are not eligible."
rows.chain: three organisations

rows.programme: HUD Rural Capacity Building for Community Development and Affordable Housing Grants (RCB)
rows.federal_agency: HUD Office of Community Planning and Development
rows.money_goes_to: National 501(c)(3) non-profits with rural capacity-building experience in at least eight of HUD's federal regions
rows.nonprofit_door: The national non-profits that win awards; HUD's listing does not name them
rows.federal_page_says: "Only National Organizations that are 501(c)(3) nonprofits, other than institutions of higher education, may apply."
rows.chain: five awards expected

rows.programme: National Park Service Paul Bruhn Historic Revitalization Grants
rows.money_goes_to: Prime grantees: State Historic Preservation Offices, Tribal Historic Preservation Offices, Certified Local Governments and non-profits
rows.nonprofit_door: The prime grantees, which run their own subgrant competitions for rural historic properties; the owner of a single historic building applies to a prime
rows.federal_page_says: "Prime grantees cannot use grant funds for their own properties or submit applications for individual buildings."

rows.programme: NHPRC State Board Programming Grants
rows.federal_agency: National Historical Publications and Records Commission (National Archives)
rows.money_goes_to: State Historical Records Advisory Boards authorised by a state, a territory or the District of Columbia
rows.nonprofit_door: The State Historical Records Advisory Board, where it uses its grant for regrants to archival repositories
rows.federal_page_says: A local archive or non-profit cannot apply to the Commission; where its state board offers regrants, it applies to the board
rows.chain: up to 20 grants

rows.programme: FEMA Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC), in outline
rows.money_goes_to: States, the District of Columbia, territories and tribes
rows.nonprofit_door: The state, territory or tribe, which applies to FEMA on behalf of its subapplicants
rows.federal_page_says: Subapplicants are local governments, cities, counties, special district governments and Tribal Nations; private non-profits are not listed as subapplicants

rows.programme: DOE Renew America's Nonprofits (energy efficiency grants for non-profit buildings)
rows.money_goes_to: Prime recipients, each a non-profit that assembles a portfolio of buildings; one round, in 2023
rows.nonprofit_door: The prime recipients selected in 2023, which distribute subawards to non-profit building owners
rows.federal_page_says: A building owner takes part as a subrecipient of a prime recipient, with subawards of up to $200,000
rows.chain: 5 to 15 prime recipients

rows.programme: AmeriCorps Volunteer Generation Fund
rows.money_goes_to: State Service Commissions only
rows.nonprofit_door: The State Service Commission of the organisation's state
rows.federal_page_says: "This opportunity is only open to State Service Commissions."; the listing does not say how a commission passes the money on

rows.programme: Strengthening Historically Black Colleges and Universities (Title III, Part B)
rows.federal_agency: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Postsecondary Education
rows.money_goes_to: Each eligible historically Black college or university, by formula; there is no national competition
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. Only Part B institutions are eligible; a non-profit that is not such an institution may not apply
rows.federal_page_says: An institution on the list in 34 CFR 608.2 files a two-phase application for a five-year grant period
rows.chain: 110 awards for FY 2026

rows.programme: Strengthening Historically Black Graduate Institutions (Title III, Part B, section 326)
rows.federal_agency: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Postsecondary Education
rows.money_goes_to: The institutions named in section 326 of the Higher Education Act, by formula
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. Only the institutions named in the statute may receive a grant
rows.federal_page_says: Funds are distributed by formula to the named institutions; not more than one grant goes to any institution in a fiscal year
rows.chain: 24 named institutions

rows.programme: Master's Degree Programs at Historically Black Colleges and Universities
rows.federal_agency: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Postsecondary Education
rows.money_goes_to: Historically Black colleges and universities, as a non-competitive grant; the list of eligible institutions was not read
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. The Department lists the programme among its non-competitive grants
rows.federal_page_says: The Department lists the programme as non-competitive; no notice was found for FY 2026

rows.programme: Strengthening Tribally Controlled Colleges and Universities (Title III, Part A, section 316, and Part F)
rows.federal_agency: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Postsecondary Education
rows.money_goes_to: Tribally controlled colleges and universities, by formula, with a minimum of $500,000 for each institution
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. Only tribal colleges and universities are eligible; a non-profit that is not such an institution may not apply
rows.federal_page_says: A new applicant first needs an eligibility determination from the Bureau of Indian Education; applications go through Grants.gov

rows.programme: Agricultural Research at 1890 Land-grant Institutions (Evans-Allen)
rows.money_goes_to: The 1890 land-grant institutions, including Tuskegee University and West Virginia State University, as capacity (formula) funds
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. Only the 1890 institutions may apply; there is no national competition
rows.federal_page_says: "Eligibility is limited to the cooperating institutions, most of which are 1862, 1890, and 1994 land-grant institutions."

rows.programme: 1890 Facilities Grants Program
rows.money_goes_to: The named 1890 land-grant institutions; the grant is noncompetitive
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. Only the 19 named 1890 institutions may apply
rows.federal_page_says: The grant is noncompetitive and restricted to the 19 named institutions; the notice shown dates from fiscal year 2023
rows.chain: 19 named institutions

rows.programme: Tribal College Endowment Program
rows.money_goes_to: Each 1994 land-grant institution, as a yearly allotment from the interest on an endowment fund
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. Only 1994 land-grant institutions receive the allotment
rows.federal_page_says: "This grant provides funds for use at the 1994 Land-grants' discretion."

rows.programme: NIFA Hatch Act capacity grants (State Agricultural Experiment Stations)
rows.money_goes_to: State Agricultural Experiment Stations, by statutory formula
rows.nonprofit_door: None named: the record's route is direct. No other college and no non-profit may apply
rows.federal_page_says: Each station answers a yearly request for applications through Grants.gov to receive its share
rows.chain: State Agricultural Experiment Stations in the 50 states, the District of Columbia and the U.S. insular areas
